novelty.basis: Contributes an original multi-mode exact-arithmetic verification framework (FFT-EXP-HALF-CERT-1.0) and constructive Lean 4 kernel auditing the finite mechanisms of preprint [6], while explicitly claiming no new asymptotic bounds beyond [6] and classical algebraic identities [2,7,8].

reproducibility.basis: Reports deterministic verification across five independent gates—Lean 4.35.0 compilation, AST float/division scan, 16 canonical JSON certificates, 70 pytest checks, and SHA-256 manifest—alongside explicit worked arithmetic witnesses, though code artifacts are external to the PDF.

rigor.basis: Combines a zero-float, zero-true-division Python exact verifier over Z, Q, and F_p with 18 constructive Lean 4.35.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) and 52 adversarial forgery checks; tempered because several Lean theorems (e.g., Thms. 11–13, 18) certify fixed small instances rather than arbitrary parameters.

significance.basis: Establishes a reliable, auditable sanity-check and witness corpus (C01–C16) for the finite-dimensional core of [6], though it explicitly excludes Grassmannian closure, Hoeffding tail bounds, prime-number-theorem length selection, and the full end-to-end recursion of Theorem 1.1.

potential_errors: In Definition 1 Mode 3(c), the Vandermonde check expression is typeset with the wide hat spanning PX rather than P\hat{X}, unlike the consistent \hat{X} and \hat{Z} notation in g(P)\hat{X} - P\hat{Z} + z\hat{Z} = z\hat{X}.

Table 2 labels C14 as "\ell=2 (F_5)" and C15 as "\ell=3 (F_7)" without clarifying in the table/caption that F_5 and F_7 apply to the query-product kernel whereas the reported Hamming Gram ranks (2 and 4) are over F_\ell (F_2 and F_3).
Reference [6] leaves "fourier" lowercase in the title ("finite fourier transforms"), inconsistent with capitalization elsewhere in the manuscript.
strengths: Clear and disciplined Honest Scope Boundary (Abstract and Section 1) that accurately delineates verified finite-dimensional identities and witnesses from unformalized asymptotic, topological, and recursive arguments in [6].

Exact zero-floating-point verification design over Z, Q, and F_p (enforcing AST float/division bans, lowest-terms bounded rationals, duplicate-key rejection) paired with 18 constructive Lean 4.35.0 theorems free of sorry and Classical.choice.

All worked arithmetic witnesses (C03, C05, C07, C11, C12, C16) and summary metrics across Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–3 are mathematically exact and mutually consistent upon independent hand verification.

Comprehensive adversarial testing mindset (52 forgery/edge-case tests out of 70 pytest checks) targeting subtle soundness failures such as non-primitive roots, off-midpoint force splits, and unlisted errors outside J.
strong_novelty_candidates: Zero-float, multi-mode exact certificate protocol (FFT-EXP-HALF-CERT-1.0) unifying finite-field spectral repair, Potter linearization, nilpotent time expansion, and Bluestein chirp verification alongside a constructive Lean 4.35.0 kernel.
summary: This companion verification manuscript introduces FFT-EXP-HALF-CERT-1.0, an exact-arithmetic Python certificate verifier (over Z, Q, and F_p) and an 18-theorem constructive Lean 4.35.0 kernel auditing finite-dimensional algebraic, geometric, and spectral-repair mechanisms extracted from OpenAI's November 24, 2026 preprint [6]. Across 16 canonical certificates (C01–C16) and four verification modes, the paper covers rectangle excess and force-disk midpoint rigidity, two-phase controlled swaps, nilpotent feedback time expansions and echelon row quotients, central-window binary parity predictors, Potter matrix linearizations, Hermite double-root spectral repair, query-product kernels, Hamming-distance Gram ranks, and Bluestein chirp convolution. All hand-verifiable identities, worked numerical witnesses, tables, and figures in the PDF are exact and internally consistent, and the paper states an explicit Honest Scope Boundary noting that asymptotic and topological arguments in [6] are not formalized.
weaknesses: As a companion verification artifact, the work does not establish new mathematical theorems or formalize the full end-to-end asymptotic bounds (e.g., Theorem 1.1 recursion, Grassmannian closure, Hoeffding tails, or PNT length selection) of [6].

Several Lean 4 theorems in Table 1 certify fixed small parameters (e.g., Theorem 11 for m=3, Theorem 12 for 2x2 Potter matrices, Theorem 13 for \ell=2 Hermite factorization, Theorem 18 for linear product-gate terms) rather than general parametric families, leaving higher-parameter cases audited only at concrete certificate sizes (e.g., W<=9, m<=5).

Table 1 includes Lean Theorems 5, 9, and 10 (Lem. 3.1 and Sec. 3.4) whose exact statements and notation (e.g., V_-(QU)) are not explained in the main text, making the manuscript slightly reliant on external preprint [6] for context.
From the PDF alone, external Lean compilation, Python verifier runs, and SHA-256 manifests cannot be independently executed, though the worked arithmetic witnesses are fully checkable by hand.
